cells.tense: Right now you are picking a direction, and the picking is steady rather than strained.
cells.ask: Say out loud to one person what you are aiming at this year, then let them ask one question about it without defending your answer.
cells.core:
You know which calling is yours and you are following it in company. It does not announce itself loudly. It shows up as being able to stay pointed at something while other people stay pointed at something else, without either of you converting or drifting.

That is the part that is working. When you say what matters to you, it arrives as something to hear rather than something to agree with, and people can feel the difference. You are pointed, and you are still in the room.

Keep it fed. A direction held this way stays real through contact, not through certainty — one conversation where you say it plainly and hear what comes back. Let someone in on what you are aiming at while it is still forming. Nothing about it needs to be finished for that to be worth doing.
cells.sheetLine: You are pointed somewhere and still in the room with people.
cells.verb: choosing which calling to follow and letting the other lights go
cells.place: beside someone where two different lives are trying to line up

cells.tense: You are standing in a future where the choice is already proven, and arguing for it before it has had time to form.
cells.ask: Pick the one direction you are most sure about, say it once today to someone who disagrees, then go do something else.
cells.core:
Somewhere ahead of you is the version where this was obviously right and the people around you can see it. You are living there already, so a conversation turns into a case you are building for a decision that has not finished happening.

The sureness is ahead of the evidence. You are explaining a light other people cannot see yet, and the explaining eats the time the direction needed to grow. You can feel it in the way you brace before someone answers.

The way back is not to doubt the calling. It is to let it stay unproven for now — one person, one true sentence about what you are aiming at, no follow-up to close the loop. What they do with it is theirs. A direction held loosely survives; one that has to be proved does not.

cells.tense: You knew what you were aiming at once, and that knowing sits behind you, in a room you have already left.
cells.ask: Tell one person what you actually want next, in plain words, and let them hear it without softening it into something safer.
cells.core:
There is a direction you carry somewhere in you, and it has stopped moving. You can still feel the edge of it when someone else names what they want — that pull, that recognition — and then it goes quiet again in you.

What is missing is not desire. It is the pointing. In company you keep yourself a little off to the side, agreeable, tuning to what other people are aiming at instead of naming your own. The connection stays warm and the alignment does not quite complete, because there is no direction of yours in the room to line up with.

Start smaller than you think. One person, one plain sentence about what you want next — not a plan, just a direction. What comes back stays theirs; the saying is yours, and it is the part that has gone unused.

cells.tense: You are already steering people toward something, and you talk about it as if the steering were the situation itself.
cells.ask: Name one thing you have been quietly directing in a relationship and say out loud that this was your call.
cells.core:
You are already pointing the people around you at something. In how you listen, what you bring up, which questions you ask and which you let pass — a direction is running, and it started with you.

What is missing is the owning. You would describe the same thing as just being realistic, or as what the situation calls for, or as nothing in particular. But the pointing is happening, and the people close to you feel its shape even when you do not say where it goes.

Owning it does not mean announcing it to a room. It means saying it once, plainly, to yourself or to the person it affects — this is what you have been steering toward. The direction was not the problem. Saying it was your call is the part that has not happened yet, and it is smaller than it looks.
cells.sheetLine: You are already steering this. You just have not said so.
